questions.subject: ART_HISTORY
questions.topic: Why a wood panel is coated before painting
questions.learningObjective: Identify why a wood panel receives a coating before painting
questions.stem: A workplace report on a Renaissance panel notes a white ground beneath the paint; what does that ground give the painter to work on?

options.text: A smooth, sealed surface that keeps paint from sinking into the wood
options.misconception: treats the ground as only a color layer

options.text: A coloured tint that sets the overall mood of the picture
A sealed, even surface that keeps paint from sinking into the wood
A rough tooth that grips the brush more firmly
options.misconception: confuses a ground with a textured primer

questions.explanation: The ground seals the wood and provides an even, non-absorbent surface so paint sits on top rather than sinking in. Option A names a similar idea but mislabels its purpose.
questions.hint: Think about what bare wood would do to paint.

questions.stem: A workplace report asks why a painter laid charcoal lines before applying colour; what does an underdrawing do for the finished work?

answer.exemplar: An underdrawing plans the composition and fixes placement of figures and forms before colour is applied, so the painter can adjust design cheaply and keep the final painting coherent.

questions.explanation: The underdrawing establishes composition and placement before paint commits the design. It lets the artist revise cheaply.
questions.hint: Think of it as the plan under the paint.

questions.subject: ART_HISTORY
questions.topic: Why a fresco wall is painted in daily sections
questions.learningObjective: Explain why fresco is painted in daily sections

stimulus.body: A workplace report describes a painter who laid fresh plaster each morning and painted before it dried. By afternoon the plaster had set and new work stopped.

questions.stem: Why is a fresco wall painted in daily sections according to the report?

options.text: Because daylight fades before large areas can be painted
Because the plaster dries and can no longer take pigment
Because the patron demanded a new design each day
Because the artist needed rest between colour mixes

questions.explanation: Fresco pigment bonds only to wet plaster, so each day's painted area must be finished before the plaster sets. Daylight is not the limiting factor.

questions.topic: Why painting on dry plaster is less durable
questions.learningObjective: Explain why painting on dry plaster is less durable
questions.stem: A workplace report compares a fresco painted on wet plaster with one painted on dry plaster; which is less durable and why?

options.text: Neither, because varnish protects both equally
The wet-plaster one, because moisture weakens the wall
Both are equal, because plaster absorbs paint either way
The dry-plaster one, because pigment sits on the surface and flakes

questions.explanation: Paint on dry plaster bonds only to the surface and flakes away, while fresco pigment fuses into wet plaster. Moisture does not weaken the wall here.
questions.hint: Which painting is fused into the plaster?

questions.stem: A workplace report compares 2 fresco panels; if 1 is wet and 1 dry, how many are less durable?
questions.explanation: Only the dry-plaster panel is less durable, so 1. Wet plaster fresco is durable.

questions.subject: ART_HISTORY
questions.topic: Why a tempera panel was finished in oil
questions.learningObjective: Justify finishing tempera in oil

stimulus.body: A workplace report shows a tempera panel with an oil glaze that deepens the shadows and enriches colour. The underlayers remain tempera.

questions.stem: Why was the panel finished in oil according to the report?

options.text: To hide the underdrawing
To make it dry before the patron arrived
To reduce the cost of pigments
To deepen colour and enrich shadows

questions.explanation: The oil glaze deepens colour and enriches shadows over tempera. It is not about drying speed or cost.

questions.subject: ART_HISTORY
questions.topic: How a glaze produces depth of colour
questions.learningObjective: Apply glaze layering in a report
questions.stem: A workplace report recommends building depth with glazes; how many thin layers should be used?

options.text: One thick opaque layer
Several thin transparent layers
No layers, just varnish
Alternating random thicknesses

questions.explanation: Several thin transparent layers build optical depth. One thick layer blocks light and fails.

questions.subject: ART_HISTORY
questions.topic: What an imprimatura does to hue
questions.learningObjective: Predict imprimatura's hue effect
questions.stem: A workplace report uses a warm imprimatura under a cool paint; what hue effect results?

options.text: The paint turns grey and dull
The warm wash disappears entirely
The cool paint reads warmer and unified
No effect on hue at all

questions.explanation: A warm imprimatura tints cool paint, making it read warmer and more unified. It does not vanish or grey.
questions.hint: The wash tints what lies over it.

questions.stem: A workplace report finds 3 crack networks on a panel; if 1 is age-related and 2 are impact, how many indicate ageing?

questions.subject: ART_HISTORY
questions.topic: How a later varnish gives itself away
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a varnish's date

stimulus.body: A workplace report on a panel finds a varnish layer lying over cracked and dirt-encrusted paint. The varnish looks fresh and glossy.

questions.stem: What does the report conclude about the varnish?

options.text: It is the original varnish
It was applied later, after ageing
It proves the painting is modern
It has no dating value

questions.explanation: A varnish over cracked, dirt-encrusted paint must be later. Stratigraphy gives its date away.
questions.hint: Look at what lies beneath it.

questions.topic: How a canvas support changes the drawing
questions.learningObjective: Synthesise canvas support effects
questions.stem: A workplace report must summarise how canvas changes drawing; what is the best summary?

options.text: Canvas has no effect on handling
Canvas forces tiny precise detail
Canvas invites broader, looser, more gestural marks
Canvas only affects colour, not drawing

questions.explanation: Canvas encourages broader, looser, gestural marks. It does not force tiny detail or only affect colour.

questions.topic: The constraint that shaped the icon
questions.learningObjective: Synthesise icon constraints
